text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The 1996 current account deficit of 59.5 billion crowns accounted for about 10.2 percent of the expected 1996 GDP. If repayments of Russian debts to Slovakia through deliveries of goods are excluded from the trade balance, the current account deficit would account for 8.74 percent of the GDP.

- Central bank Governor Vladimir Masar said restructuring of bank loan portfolios would require some 15 billion crowns. The restructuring should be carried out by creating sufficient reserves to cover classified loans and the process could take two to three years, Masar said.
- The private sector accounted for about 83 percent of the construction production in 1996.
- State-run aluminium producer ZSNP Ziar Nad Hronom plans to create two joint-ventures with unspecified foreign firms to produce aluminium wires and castings for the auto industry.

- The state Fund of Market Regulation (SFTR), which manages the state's food and grain reserves, said Slovakia would have to import about 100,000 tonnes of grain to cover consumption. The state budget will subsidise the grain imports with some 600 million crowns to prevent an increase in domestic prices.
PRAVDA - State-owned Slovak Railways (ZRS) said it would have to lay off 10,000 people due to lower transport needs both in the passenger and cargo sectors.
NARODNA OBRODA - The government is scheduled to discuss a development strategy for the capital market at its regular session on Tuesday.
- Only 4,419 privatisation bonds have been sold in anonymous auctions since the beginning of the year, out of a total of 336,000 sell orders.
SME - President Michal Kovac must set the date for the referendum on Slovakia's membership in NATO by the end of this week.

- Two coalition parties, Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's senior Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) and the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), have so far not made public their opinions on how citizens should vote in the upcoming referendum on NATO, while the other junior partner, the extreme-left Workers Party (ZRS), said people should vote against it.
